axes.name: Hook & retention
axes.rationale: The current opening immediately presents a large capped pen between differently shaped report and first-draft sheets. The opener strip and 0/4.8-second frames show a strong silhouette change, while later cap handling and permanent ink fulfill the object promise. The company/ownership exposition at roughly 6.5-37.8 seconds remains the main sag: moving labels and props carry more of this stretch than consequential action. Report examination and draft refinement supply substantive later work; the final comparison is useful but repeats the thesis. These observations remain in the same score band as my prior card.

axes.name: Illustration craft & detail
axes.rationale: The current pen has crisp oxblood shading, nickel collar, split nib, clip and rim cues; the report tabs, copper desk and green sleeves have depth and contact shading within the flat-vector style. Lamp and broad background planes remain plainer than the hero pen. The actual 56.5-, 81- and 116.5-second frames still show partly transparent hands overlapping solid props, which weakens physical solidity and character/prop finish parity. Current rendered evidence warrants the same craft score.

axes.name: Motion & animation craft
axes.rationale: The eight current strips show real cap separation, rotation and posting, distinct movement of report and attached record sheets, and a nib stroke whose ink remains after lift. The added cap-contact strip makes the final seated state readable; this is a physical change, not merely a camera transform. Several hand actions still translate a largely fixed finger pose, and translucent hands participate in the uncap, posting and ending motions. Continuous gentle bobbing provides activity without always adding intention. These strengths and limitations remain consistent with my previous 7.2; no different animation standard is being introduced.

axes.name: Composition & staging
axes.rationale: The current cabinet intake, record cutaway, drafting desk, cap insert and overhead review are intelligible and preserve important action above the caption band. The composition still repeatedly centers title, stacked labels, hero and source rail in the same broad beige field; Jumpstarter taxonomy plates compete with its desk action. The ending repeats its question in headline, center copy and caption. These are within-style hierarchy limitations rather than unsafe crops, and support retaining the prior 7.5.

axes.name: Color & grade
axes.rationale: Current cream, copper, petrol and oxblood form a coherent office palette with warm/cool contrast and shaded hero materials. Although warm neutrals recur in the historical anchors, the oxblood pen and copper/petrol dominance make this a distinct balance rather than a palette-repeat blocker. The recurring green footer wave and broad beige field still feel more like common packaging than a singular color world. The current color evidence supports the previous score.

axes.name: Typography & captions
axes.rationale: Full-resolution current frames retain readable display headings, mono labels and high-contrast open captions; timing and actual-render checks pass. Credits at 125 and 130 seconds display the required source, visit, composer and license rows without clipping, with a verified 10-second readable window. Some stacked labels remain static and over-explanatory, and the fading logic/report plates at 56.5 seconds are weak even though that spoken point is clearly captioned. The same typography score remains appropriate.

axes.name: Sound design & mix
axes.rationale: This assessment uses fresh encoded measurements, the complete 40-event schedule with rendered onset times, current strips and visible credits, not human listening. The master measures -14.33 LUFS, -2.74 dBTP and 7.4 LU range; all gates pass. The event schedule now separates move starts from contact events, notably placing the cap snap at 81.983 seconds, consistent with the rendered seated-cap sequence, and records 29 verified audible effects. This provides slightly stronger objective support for motivated sonification than the prior card. Composer/license credit is legible. Musical fit, timbral finesse and perceptual ducking remain unconfirmed by direct listening, so the increase is only 0.1.

axes.name: VO–illustration sync & entertainment
axes.rationale: The current narration and captions name the actual visible retrieval, report examination and draft refinement. At 94.5 seconds the nib touches the growing burgundy line; at 97.5 seconds it has lifted and the mark persists. Report examination and generated-section refinement supply two different professional actions, making the final act more than a postponed label reveal. The long context section and dense mechanism labels remain procedural rather than gripping. The evidence supports retaining 7.7.

axes.name: Accuracy & sourcing
axes.rationale: The current script, post, claims and verified source register keep the September 11 KGS support announcement distinct from the earlier AWS Army case study. The pictured DORA workflow is API retrieval plus prebuilt logic; separately labeled Jumpstarter uses language models on Bedrock for initial document sections. Professional review/refinement is source-backed, the workflow is visibly illustrative, and there is no invented error, autonomous award, net-productivity proof or quantified Alaska return. Vendor publication and KGS reproduction do not constitute independent performance validation. The current claims remain strong and bounded at the prior score.

axes.name: Alaska authenticity & cultural respect
axes.rationale: KGS and Koniag are named corporations, with the Kodiak regional connection accurately scoped. The current ordinary office hands and objects do not borrow Native iconography, impersonate a Native community or use savior framing. No local deployment, jobs or financial return is invented. The generic office is appropriate to this corporate workflow story, though it offers little additional specifically Alaskan texture. The current evidence supports the same 8.5.

axes.name: Writing & post quality
axes.rationale: The current 204-word VO preserves the pen promise, credit for useful preparation, a clear report/draft distinction and a closing question earned by visible professional work. The exact current post opens with a professional-decision hook and ends with specific report checks or draft changes readers could discuss. Both retain attribution and scope. The full DORA expansion and repeated preparation/completion wording add some burden. These are the same strengths and small writing limitations recorded in my prior card, freshly checked here.
